To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AhR and β-catenins cooperate in the transcriptional regulation of selected genes, but the persistent activation of AhR interferes with the Wnt/ β-catenin pathway and disrupts the liver progenitor cell phenotype.
AhR and β-catenins interact in liver progenitor cells and this interaction is important in the regulation of liver progenitor cell differentiation.
the activation of AhRs by TCDD leads to a downregulatation of Wnt/ß-catenin signaling and an inhibition of cell differentiation of liver progenitor cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interactions between AhR and WNT/β-catenins signaling pathways and their role in the regulation of liver progenitor cell fate.
the interplay between AhR and WNT signaling in the liver.
the interactions of the arylhydrocarbon receptor (Ah) and Wnt/ß-catenin signaling pathways, which are important for liver development and regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interplay of the Wnt/ß-catenin pathway with the AhR signaling network in the progenitors of the liver is complex and may be cell-type specific.
the AhR and β-catenins are not only interacting partners but that they are also involved in a complex regulatory network in the liver.
the interplay of the Wnt/ β-catenin pathway with the AhR is a complex one and the outcome of this interplay may depend on both cell type and the AhR activation status.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activation of Ah receptor may have a dual effect on liver progenitor cells: it can enhance their proliferation by increasing expression of some target genes but it can also decrease their stemness by downregulating expression of some other genes.
AhR is an important player in Wnt/β- catenin signaling and that this signaling may play a role in the regulation of AhR-dependent transcription.
the AhR and β-catenins are not only interacting in transcriptional regulation, but that the AhR can also affect β-catenin-mediated cell-cell interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of Ah receptor can lead to a downregualtion of the Wnt/ß-catenin pathway.
AhR activation may have a profound effect on Wnt/βcatenin signaling and cell-cell adhesion in liver progenitors.
the AhR is an important regulator of Wnt signaling, and that the AhR may be used as a tool to modulate Wnt/βcatenin signaling in the context of liver development, regeneration and disease.
